precise_scope: For every connected smooth compact Kahler n-fold, pseudoeffective zero-volume class and actual theta-psh reference psi, the bounded singularity-type domain has an exact actual-current degree d<n, mixed current vanishing, the positive raw-mass operator <T_u^d> wedge omega^(n-d) on X, and sufficient rescaled perturbation convergence with sup-distance o(epsilon). Its bounded relative primitive has a cocycle and depends only on the auxiliary class; the leading energy limit holds for arbitrary representatives of converging Kahler classes and sup-distance tending to zero. The operator extends to more-singular degree-d relative full-mass currents and is continuous under decreasing full-mass sequences, including bounded-type truncations. This does not close the unchanged original P15.2.
limitations: No general intrinsic geometric d-dimensional carrier or quotient is constructed; the carrier of the measure is the n-dimensional X.
No characterization of minimum necessary reference data is proved. This measure requires a full Kahler form, and a same-class analytic example proves its dependence.
Operator perturbation convergence requires bounded-type differences o(epsilon), with a fixed form or smooth positive limit; arbitrary perturbations are not covered.
General unbounded finite-energy truncation-value continuity, numerical cocycles and reference change are unproved; weak measure convergence gives no weighted tail estimate.
Degree-d finite joint energy has not been shown here to control weighted degrees k<d or joint unbounded perturbation limits.
The actual-type degree is not identified with the class numerical dimension.

result.report:
The stated Theorems A and B satisfy the scoped completion criteria. This verdict does not establish the unchanged original P15.2, an intrinsic lower-dimensional carrier, unrestricted perturbation independence, or an unbounded energy cocycle. Those stronger assertions are explicitly excluded. The draft’s label “partial” is consistent with this distinction.

The degree argument is valid. M₀=∫ωⁿ>0. The current P+εω is strictly positive, so its class is big. Comparing it with a minimal-singularity current gives ∫⟨(P+εω)ⁿ⟩≤vol(α+ε[ω]). Positive multilinearity expands the left side into the stated nonnegative polynomial. Its constant term Mₙ must vanish because the right side tends to zero. Thus d<n. Pointwise comparison of Kähler forms preserves positivity or vanishing of every Mₖ. Bounded-type mixed mass equality, with smooth forms filling the remaining slots, proves anchor invariance and all asserted mixed masses. For k>d, their zero Kähler trace forces the positive product current itself to vanish. Mass monotonicity proves the same vanishing for more-singular factors in the same class. None of these steps identifies d with the class numerical dimension.

The signed integration-by-parts applications have the required hypotheses. Every current R used in Sections 4–6 is closed, positive, of bidegree (n−1,n−1), and has no pluripolar trace mass. The directions are bounded differences of quasi-psh functions whose polar loci are therefore R-negligible. Smooth tests and smooth reference potentials are admissible. Relative association and additivity identify each signed insertion with the stated difference of ordinary products; a common sufficiently large Kähler background can be added to the quasi-psh representatives and then cancels. Consequently no signed product is being inferred from unsupported multilinearity for arbitrary distributions.

The normalization and gradient corrections are harmless for these applications. DDNL’s source potential is u/(2π), and the convention in Vu’s relative-product source uses u/2. For the latter conversion, each side of integration by parts with source differences v/2,w/2 is half the corresponding displayed expression, including its gradient term. The intrinsic identity is dv∧dᶜv=(1/2)ddᶜ(v²)−vddᶜv. With a=φ₁,k+ρ and b=φ₂,k+ρ, the correct local expression is [ddᶜ(a²)+ddᶜ(b²)−(1/2)ddᶜ((a+b)²)−vₖddᶜvₖ]∧R. Positive local psh squares give the required locality, and Stokes gives the uniform gradient mass bound 2‖vₖ‖∞∫κ∧R. For the cutoff χₖ, choose ρ so χₖ+ρ is positive psh and increases to 1+ρ outside the R-negligible complete pluripolar set. Weighted Bedford–Taylor convergence, followed by expansion of this expression, gives χₖddᶜχₖ∧R→0. Bounded convergence also gives ddᶜ(χₖ²)∧R→0. The correct half-factor identity therefore still makes the cutoff gradient tend to zero, and Cauchy–Schwarz eliminates the boundary terms. This checks both IBP symmetry and the positive gradient used for concavity.

The operator estimates are established with their stated rates. For fixed u, the binomial expansion leaves precisely μᵤ,ω plus positive lower-degree terms after division by binom(n,d)εⁿ⁻ᵈ. Their total mass is O(ε) when d≥1; for d=0 the equality with ωⁿ is exact. For varying potentials, both Sε and Aε belong to the same perturbed class and bounded singularity type. Factorization and admissible IBP give the stated sum of ∫hεddᶜf∧Rⱼ,ε. Each trace mass is exactly Σₖ≤d binom(n−1,k)εⁿ⁻¹⁻ᵏMₖ, hence O(εⁿ⁻ᵈ⁻¹). This yields O(δε/ε) against each fixed smooth test. Uniform rescaled mass bounds extend convergence to continuous tests. Smoothly converging positive auxiliary forms give uniform comparison and test constants. The proof does not use a fibration estimate or a universal θ-bound on arbitrary X-tests.

The bounded primitive and its regularity assertions follow. Positive multilinearity gives polynomial coefficient integrals on each finite convex hull. IBP makes the derivative of its one-form symmetric. The hull has nonempty relative interior in its affine span, so the symmetry identity extends to the polynomial extension; Stokes on triangles proves segment independence. The beta integral produces exactly the factor 1/(d+1), establishing the formula, anchor cocycle and variation along the specified finite-dimensional C¹ paths. Positivity and constant mass M_d give monotonicity, the M_d Lipschitz bound and constant shifts. The second segment derivative equals minus d times the finite positive intrinsic gradient integral, proving concavity. Degree zero is handled separately: the primitive is affine and no negative-degree product is used.

Auxiliary representative independence of the leading primitive is proved, while measure independence is correctly rejected. The smooth ddᶜ-lemma supplies g for cohomologous Kähler forms. Factoring their power difference gives positive closed currents R of the required bidegree. IBP transfers ddᶜg to u−ψ, producing the difference of two degree-(d+1) products, both zero. This also covers d=0. Smooth changes of θ accompanied by subtraction of the same potential preserve the actual currents and differences. Bounded-equivalent anchor changes obey the already established cocycle.

The positive-ε energy coefficient calculation is valid for every index, not merely the finite diagnostic range. Counting a (k+1)-element subset by its (j+1)-st element gives Σₐ binom(a,j)binom(n−a,k−j)=binom(n+1,k+1). Thus the exact energy expansion has coefficient binom(n,k)E⁽ᵏ⁾ and stops at k=d. For uε, the perturbed-background cocycle gives an error at most δεmε, where mε is the actual anchor mass polynomial. Its rescaled value stays bounded, so δε→0 suffices for energy. This estimate does not require uε to be θ-psh before perturbation and does not replace actual mass by class volume.

The arbitrary-representative, converging-class energy assertion is also established. Closedness makes every Mₖ a continuous cohomological polynomial, giving uniform bounds despite uncontrolled representatives. The bounded weight bounds each lower energy coefficient by ‖u−ψ‖∞Mₖ. After rescaling, all k<d terms vanish. Representative independence allows the leading coefficient to be evaluated using fixed smooth affine representatives near the limiting Kähler class, where it is a finite polynomial and hence continuous. The same class bounds control the varying-potential energy error. This establishes only the claimed energy limit, not a corresponding operator limit with arbitrary representatives.

Theorem B has a complete measure-convergence argument. Interpret its potentials as θ-psh, as required throughout the current construction, and normalize u≤ψ. Monotonicity sandwiches every intermediate mixed mass between the equal masses of u and ψ. The truncations max(u,ψ−j) are therefore bounded-type θ-psh full-mass majorants and decrease to u. Their local psh potentials converge in L¹ by domination with the integrable difference p₁−p. The constant smooth relative background satisfies the required convergence condition. Local lower semicontinuity implies that every weak cluster measure dominates μᵤ,ω; equal mass M_d makes that positive difference zero. The identical argument proves continuity for decreasing full-mass sequences and the stated majorants. If the bare (d,d) product current is also intended by “actual-current operator,” apply the same lower semicontinuity with relative background 1 and complementary positive test forms: cluster currents dominate ⟨Tᵤᵈ⟩, and their equal Kähler trace again forces equality. Degree zero is immediate. Closedness proves invariance of the full-mass condition under cohomologous auxiliary representatives.

The finite-energy supporting assertions are correctly scoped. In Vu’s definitions, take m=d≥1, P in every slot, χ(t)=t and R=ωⁿ⁻ᵈ. On connected compact X, equality of the top-degree cohomology classes is equivalent to mass equality. The joint linear energy is proportional to dΣₐ binom(d,a)∫(ψ−u)⟨TᵤᵃPᵈ⁻ᵃ⟩ωⁿ⁻ᵈ, with the stated factor 1/2 under the source potential convention. Finiteness therefore matches the displayed domain. The published convexity and bounded-reference invariance apply. No weighted truncation continuity, unbounded cocycle or unbounded perturbation limit is inferred from them.

Both geometric examples check out. On the product of projective lines, a cohomologous perturbation on the second factor changes η_y∧ω by the nonzero signed measure tη_y∧ddᶜg while preserving mass. The divisor current has zero nonpluripolar degree-one product, although its nef class has numerical dimension one. The logarithmic subpower example has positive radial Hessian, zero atomic mass at the puncture, and finite weighted tail precisely because ∫∞s²ᵃ⁻²ds converges for a<1/2. It provides the asserted unbounded finite-energy full-mass example. The carrier statements concern the ambient manifold X; they assert neither full support nor a geometric quotient of dimension d.

Additional harmless source corrections should be explicit. BEGZ Lemma 1.5 needs cutoff indicators tending to 1, for example increasing cutoff sets; the union condition alone does not imply this. Every cutoff use relevant here has the required property. Vu’s Lemma 2.5 refers to the vanishing bracketed differences, rather than individual uncancelled summands. In the relative closedness proof, the missing half-factor and omitted Cauchy–Schwarz square roots are corrected by the intrinsic identity and the usual square-root estimate; bounded first factors and vanishing second factors give the same conclusion. The T/T_l slip in Lemma 4.1 disappears in the constant-background application. Proposition 4.2’s m/n and subscript defects are not used in the new argument. These corrections do not change the scoped theorem or require a replacement substantive argument. Source bodies proved by reference are used only as precisely stated published foundations, as permitted by the task; proposals, previous verdicts, hashes and compilation are not mathematical premises.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler n-fold, the ordinary nonpluripolar product of p closed positive (1,1)-currents, 1≤p≤n, is well-defined, locally finite, positive, closed, symmetric, local in the plurifine topology and has no pluripolar trace mass. It is multilinear under positive additions and homogeneous under positive scalings. Multiplication by smooth closed positive forms agrees with the corresponding cutoff construction. [BEGZ, Propositions 1.4, 1.6 and Theorem 1.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2).
passages.quote: Proposition 1.6. Let T1 , ..., Tp be closed positive (1, 1)-currents on a compact Kähler manifold X. Then their non-pluripolar product hT1 ∧ ... ∧ Tp i is well-defined.

passages.statement: Every pseudoeffective real (1,1)-class on a compact Kähler manifold has a positive current with minimal singularities, less singular than every positive current in that class. In a big class β, its top nonpluripolar mass equals vol(β). For a pseudoeffective class α and any Kähler class λ, vol(α)=limε↓0 vol(α+ελ). Positive products of nef classes agree with their ordinary cup products. [BEGZ, Section 1.4 and Definition 1.17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2).
passages.quote: Such θ-psh functions with minimal singularities always exist, as was observed by Demailly.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler n-fold, for closed positive (1,1)-currents T_1,…,T_m and a closed positive (p,p)-current R with m+p≤n, their R-relative nonpluripolar product is well-defined, finite, closed, positive, symmetric and positively homogeneous. It does not charge a locally complete pluripolar set that R does not charge. Additivity in a current slot holds when R does not charge the polar loci of the added currents. Relative products associate: taking a relative product of the remaining factors with the product of a first group gives the full relative product. With relative background 1 they are ordinary nonpluripolar products. [Vu, relative-product foundations and Proposition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

For χ:R→R convex increasing with χ(−∞)=−∞, its joint weighted energy is the sum over all subsets J of integrals of −χ(Σ_j(u_j−φ_j)) against ⟨∧j∈J T_j∧∧j∉J P_j⋅∧R⟩, after choosing negative potentials with u_j≤φ_j. When all P_j=P, the diagonal full-mass and diagonal finite weighted-energy domains are convex; the finite weighted-energy domain is unchanged by replacing P with a cohomologous bounded-equivalent positive current. [Vu, Section 3, Corollary 3.2 and Theorem 3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

premises: On a compact Kähler n-fold, the ordinary nonpluripolar product of p closed positive (1,1)-currents, 1≤p≤n, is well-defined, locally finite, positive, closed, symmetric, local in the plurifine topology and has no pluripolar trace mass. It is multilinear under positive additions and homogeneous under positive scalings. Multiplication by smooth closed positive forms agrees with the corresponding cutoff construction. [BEGZ, Propositions 1.4, 1.6 and Theorem 1.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2).

Let X be a compact Kähler n-fold, θ_j smooth closed real (1,1)-forms with pseudoeffective classes, and u_j,v_j∈PSH(X,θ_j), 1≤j≤n. If v_j≤u_j+C_j for every j, then ∫X⟨(θ_1+ddc u_1)∧⋯∧(θ_n+ddc u_n)⟩≥∫X⟨(θ_1+ddc v_1)∧⋯∧(θ_n+ddc v_n)⟩. If each pair is two-sided bounded-equivalent, the masses are equal. Here the potentials and ddc are expressed consistently in the chosen normalization. [DDNL, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.4](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf).

Every pseudoeffective real (1,1)-class on a compact Kähler manifold has a positive current with minimal singularities, less singular than every positive current in that class. In a big class β, its top nonpluripolar mass equals vol(β). For a pseudoeffective class α and any Kähler class λ, vol(α)=limε↓0 vol(α+ελ). Positive products of nef classes agree with their ordinary cup products. [BEGZ, Section 1.4 and Definition 1.17](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2).

On a compact Kähler n-fold, for closed positive (1,1)-currents T_1,…,T_m and a closed positive (p,p)-current R with m+p≤n, their R-relative nonpluripolar product is well-defined, finite, closed, positive, symmetric and positively homogeneous. It does not charge a locally complete pluripolar set that R does not charge. Additivity in a current slot holds when R does not charge the polar loci of the added currents. Relative products associate: taking a relative product of the remaining factors with the product of a first group gives the full relative product. With relative background 1 they are ordinary nonpluripolar products. [Vu, relative-product foundations and Proposition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

Let R be a fixed closed positive current on U⊂Cⁿ. For locally bounded psh functions p_1,…,p_m, the weighted Bedford–Taylor product p_1 ddcp_2∧⋯∧ddcp_m∧R is continuous when each locally bounded psh approximant converges in L¹loc from above. It is also continuous for increasing approximants converging almost everywhere to the given locally bounded psh limits, provided each discrepancy set is locally complete pluripolar and is not charged by R. The products are taken in degrees not exceeding n. [Vu, Theorem 2.6 and Remark 2.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.11111v1).

Let X be a compact Kähler n-fold and R a closed positive (n−1,n−1)-current. A dsh function v is R-admissible when it has quasi-psh representatives v=φ_1−φ_2 whose polar loci are not charged by R. For bounded R-admissible dsh functions v,w, their signed relative insertions and polarized gradients are defined and finite, and ∫X w⟨ddcv⋅∧R⟩=∫X v⟨ddcw⋅∧R⟩=−∫X⟨dw∧dcv⋅∧R⟩. The intrinsic self-gradient ⟨dv∧dcv⋅∧R⟩ is positive, uses the identity dv∧dcv=(1/2)ddc(v²)−vddcv, and is independent of admissible representatives. [Vu, Lemmas 2.3–2.6 and Theorem 2.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

Let U⊂Cⁿ, let R be a fixed smooth closed positive (p,p)-form, and let p_j^(l),p_j be psh for 1≤j≤m with m+p≤n. Assume p_j^(l)≥p_j, p_j^(l)→p_j in L¹loc, and that the indicated relative nonpluripolar products are locally finite. For every compactly supported smooth weakly positive complementary test form Φ, liminfl→∞∫U⟨∧j ddcp_j^(l)⋅∧R⟩∧Φ≥∫U⟨∧j ddcp_j⋅∧R⟩∧Φ. The constant sequence R_l=R satisfies Condition (*), the local uniform mass and decreasing bounded-psh weighted-product condition required for this inequality. [Vu, Condition (*) and Lemma 4.1(i)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.11111v1).

On a compact Kähler manifold, every smooth real closed (1,1)-form whose real de Rham cohomology class is zero equals ddc g for a smooth real function g. This holds for ddc=i∂∂bar/(2π), by constant rescaling of the differential operator. [Deligne–Griffiths–Morgan–Sullivan, Section 5, Lemma 5.11](https://publications.ias.edu/sites/default/files/realhomotopytheory.pdf).

Let X be compact Kähler, R a closed positive (p,p)-current, and P_j positive currents in pseudoeffective (1,1)-classes α_j, with m+p≤dim X. The relative full-mass tuple domain consists of T_j∈α_j more singular than P_j and satisfying {⟨T_1∧⋯∧T_m⋅∧R⟩}={⟨P_1∧⋯∧P_m⋅∧R⟩}. For χ:R→R convex increasing with χ(−∞)=−∞, its joint weighted energy is the sum over all subsets J of integrals of −χ(Σ_j(u_j−φ_j)) against ⟨∧j∈J T_j∧∧j∉J P_j⋅∧R⟩, after choosing negative potentials with u_j≤φ_j. When all P_j=P, the diagonal full-mass and diagonal finite weighted-energy domains are convex; the finite weighted-energy domain is unchanged by replacing P with a cohomologous bounded-equivalent positive current. [Vu, Section 3, Corollary 3.2 and Theorem 3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.13241v3).

Vu’s arXiv:2004.11111v1 convention is dc=i(∂bar−∂)/(2π) and ddc=i∂∂bar/π. DDNL’s convention represents positive currents as θ_u=θ+i∂∂bar u. [Vu’s notation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.11111v1), [DDNL’s definition](https://msp.org/apde/2018/11-8/apde-v11-n8-p06-s.pdf).
